MINUTES
  REGULAR PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  FEBRUARY 20, 2018

A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:00 p.m. in the City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North,
Rolling Hills Estates, California by CHAIR POPE.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR POPE led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance

3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Chair Pope, Romanelli, Retz, Wroan

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Persichina, Portugal, Giglia

  STAFF PRESENT:  Andy Clark, Community Services Director
  Daniel A-Haja, Senior Recreation Leader

  Community Services Director Clark stated that new to the City this year are Student
  Commissioners and Committee Members who will observe meetings and provide input. He
  introduced Summer and Evelyn Hasama, as Student Park and Activities Commissioners.

4.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REORGANIZATION

  CHAIR POPE stated that the City Council appointed VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI to serve as
  Chairman of the Park & Activities Commission for 2018.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI, on behalf of the City, staff, and fellow Commissioner’s thanked
  COMMISSIONER POPE for her service and leadership as Park & Activities Chair and presented
  her with a plaque. Community Services Director Clark added that COMMISSIONER GIGLIA was
  appointed as Vice Chair.

5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF JANUARY 16, 2018

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that in the committee assignments, Commissioner Giglia is listed
  as representative for Traffic & Safety Committee. COMMISSIONER POPE stated that she
  expressed interest to the City Council to remain on the Traffic & Safety Committee. Community
  Services Director stated that he will make the change.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE

  TO APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF JANUARY 16,
  2018

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so moved.

6.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

7.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  NONE

8.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER ANNUAL REPORT

  Community Services Director Clark introduced Connie Smith, Education Director of the Palos
  Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy (PVPLC).

  Ms. Smith provided a brief overview of the George F Canyon Nature Center Annual Report. The
  report reflects fewer visitors last year but the numbers should improve in part due to scout
  activities that have already been booked. Ms. Smith stated funding will be received from the
  recently approved, Junior Naturalist Grant. Modifications in the offerings and activity schedules

  1
   are being reviewed as well as low cost ways to improve the aesthetics of the center are in
  progress. Community Services Director Clark added that Ms. Smith and Andrea Vona, Executive
  Director of the PVPLC are working with the L.A. Marine Mammal Exhibit – Mobile Unit on
  scheduling dates, and this should also increase the number of visitors to the George F Canyon
  Nature Center.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if the PV Water Pipeline Project will have any impact on the L.A.
  Marine Mammal Exhibit schedule. Community Services Director Clark stated that the exhibit will
  only be scheduled through May and there should be no impact since the pipeline project will begin
  after May.

  COMMISSIONER WROAN asked if there are any prior approvals needed from the City for the
  Nature Center to proceed with changes/projects described in the report. Ms. Smith stated no,
  that this was informational only. Ms. Smith stated that Community Services Director Clark has
  helped facilitate getting painters to improve their sign to include operating hours.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI asked about funding for some of the projects listed in the report. Ms. Smith
  stated that the items listed are covered within her budget.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked about the synergy between the future of the Community Center
  and the George F Canyon Nature Center. Community Services Director Clark stated that up for
  discussion at the Policy Development Session, there is a budget for a community center
  replacement study to determine what can be done to combine the buildings. More direction will
  be provided after the Policy Development Session.

  B.  5K RACE COURSE RENTAL REQUEST

  Community Services Director Clark presented the staff report for the request by Harbor Interfaith
  Services, Inc. for the rental of Ernie Howlett Park for a 5K Race on Sunday, July 1, 2018.

  Staff recommends that the Park and Activities Commission approve the Harbor Interfaith
  Services, Inc.’s use of Ernie Howlett Park and the City’s 5K race course on July 1, 2018 under
  the conditions and for the fees outlined in the report.

  Mike Radice, Director of Development, Harbor Interfaith Services, Inc., provided information on
  the services that this organization provides for the homeless and those in risk of becoming
  homeless and explained how the proceeds from this event will be used.

  Mr. Radice stated that currently they have three corporate sponsors, which are: Torrance
  Memorial Medical Center, City National Bank, and Smart & Final.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that this is a great initiative and thanked Mr. Radice for seeking the
  City of Rolling Hills Estates for the use of Ernie Howlett Park as a venue for this event.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that as it is true that the City is very welcoming for these events,
  however, she would like to make sure that the amount of events are not interfering with the
  equestrians. Community Services Director Clark stated that he will bring this up at the upcoming
  Equestrian Committee meeting. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI added notification to the Tennis
  Club.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ to,

  APPROVE THE USE OF ERNIE HOWLETT PARK AND THE CITY’S 5K RACE COURSE
  ON JULY 1, 2018 UNDER THE CONDITIONS AND FOR THE FEES OUTLINED IN
  THE REPORT AND WITH THE ADDITIONAL CONDITION THAT THE CITY PROVIDE
  PROPER NOTIFICATION TO THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE AND TENNIS CLUB.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so moved.

  C.  SUMMER MOVIE NIGHTS PROGRAM

  Community Services Director Clark presented a summary of the staff report for the Summer Movie
  Night choices.

  Staff recommends that the Park and Activities Commission determine the dates and movie
  selections for the City’s 2018 Summer Movie Night program at Ernie Howlett Park.

  Daniel A-Haja, Sr. Recreation Leader, named the top three movie sequels, as follows: Incredibles,
  Hotel Transylvania, and Ant Man.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES  2
COMMISSION MINUTES
FEBRUARY 20, 2018
   The Park and Activities Commission agreed that the movies should be kept to a rating of PG.

  COMMISSIONER E. HASANA, provided input and stated that she thinks that Incredibles is a
  good choice and agreed that it should be kept to a PG rating.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER WROAN to,

  APPROVE THE SUMMER MOVIE NIGHT PROGRAM AND TO APPROVE THE
  INCREDIBLES AND HOTEL TRANSYLVANIA SEQUELS AND AT THE NEXT PARK
  AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING PROVIDE TWO ADDITIONAL MOVIE
  CHOICES.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so moved.

  D.  PARK DESIGN SELECTION SUBCOMMITTEE

  Community Services Director Clark provided a brief summary of the staff report, including
  background on the original suggestions for the pocket park design and stated that staff is working
  on developing an RFP for this project.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that staff recommends that the Park and Activities
  Commission select up to three Commissioners to serve on the Park Design Consultant Selection
  Subcommittee to determine the most qualified firm for the design and development of a new park
  on the southwest corner of Palos Verdes Drive North and Palos Verdes Drive East.

  COMMISSIONER’S RETZ and POPE stated that they would like to serve on the subcommittee.
  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that COMMISSIONER’s PORTUGAL and PERSICHINA had
  also expressed interest in serving. CHAIR ROMANELLI stated he would like to serve if the third
  vacancy is not filled.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER WROAN to,

  APPROVE THE SELECTION OF COMMISSIONER’S RETZ AND POPE TO SERVE ON
  THE PARK DESIGN CONSULTANT SELECTION SUBCOMMITTEE WITH THE THIRD
  COMMISSIONER PENDING DECISION AT THE NEXT MEETING PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES MEETING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so moved.

  E.  MONTECILLO HOA PARKWAY LANDSCAPING SUBCOMMITTEE

  Community Services Director Clark provided a brief summary of the staff report and stated that
  the Montecillo HOA is requesting assistance in reviewing an overall plan for the Parkway
  Landscape design.

  Dave Brunnemeyer, Montecillo HOA, stated that there are many projects going on at the
  Montecillo entryway and it has been falling apart. He stated that he would like to coordinate with
  the City in order to get input on the project. Community Services Director Clark stated that there
  is money budgeted to do minor improvements that can be done in-house or by Bennett
  Landscaping. However, if the outcome is that it is a major project then it will need to be brought
  to the Park and Activities Commission for recommendation for approval by the City Council.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if the center divider in Montecillo is public or private property.
  Community Services Director stated that it is public property maintained (upon the City’s approval)
  by the Montecillo HOA.

  Mr. Brunnemeyer stated that in the past, the parkways approaching Montecillo, gave the
  impression of an entryway. Homes have been built there and that has been lost.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI volunteered and stated that the commissioners who are not present be
  notified of the opportunity.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ to,

  ADJOURN TO THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD MEETING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so moved.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES  3
COMMISSION MINUTES
FEBRUARY 20, 2018
 9.  ADJOURN TO THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD MEETING

  Community Services Director Clark provided a brief summary of the staff report.

  Staff recommends that the Pepper Tree Foundation Advisory Board make a recommendation to
  the Pepper Tree Foundation Board of Directors to approve the agreement with Michael Hogue
  Productions to provide fundraising, promotional and consulting services for the 2018 Hills Are
  Alive Race.

  Michael Hogue, MHP, expressed concern with holding another race so close to the Hills Are Alive
  Race and stated that there are too many races in the South Bay and it may cause a negative
  effect on the number of participants. Mr. Hogue stated that this is his 20th year coordinating the
  Hills Are Alive Race for the City. Every year it is increasingly difficult to secure sponsors due to
  the amount of events in the area. Mr. Hogue stated that it is difficult to get the local high schools
  to participate and some will not participate at all.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that she agrees there are too many of these races but this event
  has great value as a community event and would like to continue to promote this event as such.
  Although the lack of participation by the high schools is disappointing, she understands that their
  schedule may not allow for their participation during this time. COMMISSIONER POPE stated
  that she believes that the other race will have a different audience with different motivation for
  participating in the race.

  Mr. Hogue stated that in the past, there was better means of advertising, and now there needs to
  be more promotion done using social media. The City offers banner space, but stated that the
  policy on banners is too stringent.

  Mr. Hogue stated that there is growth with his San Pedro event from participation in women who
  walk.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that many of the issues that Mr. Hogue mentioned are items that
  could be discussed among the members of the Race Subcommittee.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER WROAN, Mr. Hogue stated that the race has
  grossed from $20K - $30K. COMMISSIONER WROAN clarified that according to the agreement,
  Mr. Hogue receives $4000 for his fee against 50% of the gross amount.

  COMMISSIONER WROAN asked what Mr. Hogue believes is the percentage that will be diluted
  from the Hills Are Alive Race. Mr. Hogue stated that it could be a couple of hundred runners
  and added that he believes they may lose local sponsors.

  COMMISSIONER WROAN stated that if after this race, there is a significant loss, then he agrees
  that approving another race was a bad decision. However, it is speculative to say this right now.

  Mr. Hogue stated that every year it is more difficult to get participants due to the number of races.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that the City has added the Pi Race and another race in the past and
  stated that he has not seen a negative effect on the Hills Are Alive Race since they have been
  added. CHAIR ROMANELLI agreed that at this time it is speculative.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that Mr. Hogue and the Subcommittee should be charged with
  the task of examining how the event can evolve and if not, examining what this event means to
  the City and the Community.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated this agreement comes before the Commission every year and does
  not recall any changes and asked if there is a need to make revisions.

  Mr. Hogue stated that the only change that he recalls is if the City secures a sponsor, he is
  responsible for servicing the sponsor and there would be no fee paid to him.

  COMMISSIONER WROAN asked it there are any sponsors that the City has secured in the past
  that are sponsors now where Mr. Hogue is compensated. Mr. Hogue stated that he has secured
  all of the sponsors for this event.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the agreement is reviewed by the City
  Attorney every year.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES  4
COMMISSION MINUTES
FEBRUARY 20, 2018
   Mr. Hogue stated that he has a database from the Conquer the Bridge Race that he uses to send
  out to promote the Hills Are Alive Race and there is no charge to the City for that. Also, he stated
  that the capacity for this race is 600 participants, anything over that does not provide for an
  enjoyable race.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI asked Mr. Hogue is he agrees with the agreement as it is. Mr. Hogue stated
  that he has no changes.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated according to COMMISSIONER WROAN, the agreement has
  gone through the proper legal channels and stated that according to CHAIR ROMANELLI this
  agreement may need to be reviewed by the Race Subcommittee to be relevant with the
  changing time.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that the Race Subcommittee will pick-up the discussion at this
  meeting regarding the agreement and the inclusion of the other races so that it is dealt with on a
  comprehensive level going forward.

  COMMISSIONER WROAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ to,

  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD OF
  DIRECTORS TO APPROVE THE AGREEMENT WITH MICHAEL HOGUE
  PRODUCTIONS TO PROVIDE FUNDRAISING, PROMOTIONAL AND CONSULTING
  SERVICES FOR THE 2018 HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE.

  AYES:  Chair Romanelli, Pope, Retz, Wroan
  NOES:
  ABSENT:  Persichina, Portugal, Giglia
  ABSTAIN:

10.  RECONVENE TO THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ to,

  RECONVENE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so moved.

11.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that there are a lot of fencing repairs needed at Highridge Park.
  Community Services Director Clark stated that in order to use grant funds, the fence needs to be
  along a bridle trail and since there is a bridle trail at Highridge Park, he will look into it. The fence
  company that the City was working with has moved to another state and staff will need to go
  before the City Council for approval to begin working with the next bidder.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that some of the post caps are missing at Dapplegray Park.

  B.  PARADE SUBCOMMITTEE DEBRIEFING MEETING UPDATE

  Community Services Director Clark stated that things are looking good for next year’s parade.
  Manhattan Beach Studios, who produced last year’s video, have a good relationship with the
  volleyball players in Manhattan Beach and there is discussion on inviting an Olympic Volleyball
  Player to serve as the Grand Marshall of the next parade.

12.  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS

  A.  SBCCOG ANNUAL GENERAL ASSEMBLY REGISTRATION DEADLINE - FEBRUARY
  15TH

  Community Services Director Clark stated that there is still time to register for the SBCCOG
  Annual General Assembly.

  B.  PENINSULA HIGH SCHOOL WALK FOR LIFE – FEBRUARY 15TH

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the Peninsula High School Walk for Life was a
  great event. They usually have approximately 500 walkers and raise approximately $50K. The
  proceeds go to the City of Hope and the American Cancer Society.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES  5
COMMISSION MINUTES
FEBRUARY 20, 2018
   C.  FORM 700 FORMS DUE – APRIL 2ND

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the Form 700’s are due April 2nd.

  D.  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK SLOPE DEAD TREE REMOVALS

  Community Services Director Clark stated that City staff and Bennett Landscaping is scheduled
  to do another sweep of the eastern slope of Hawthorne Blvd. along Ernie Howlett Park. 50% of
  dead trees have been removed and many more will be removed in the coming week.

  E.  PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST POCKET PARK DESIGN UPDATE

  Community Services Director stated that Willdan has sent a survey crew to the pocket park site
  and they will be presenting a conceptual design; possibly at the next Park and Activities
  Commission meeting.

  F.  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK PERIMETER PATHWAY PROJECT UPDATE

  Community Services Director stated that the Ernie Howlett Park Perimeter Pathway Project is set
  to begin. There is a grant of $249K to replace an approximate ¾ mile decomposed granite
  pathway around Ernie Howlett Park and install exercise equipment.

13.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JANUARY 23, 2018

  B.  PLANNING COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 5, 2018

  NO ACTION TAKEN

14.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  COMMISSIONER ROLES DURING CITYWIDE DISASTERS

  Community Services Director Clark stated that commissioner roles during citywide disasters was
  brought up at a previous meeting. Alexa Davis, Assistant to the City Manager will attend the next
  Park and Activities Commission meeting to present information on this item.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that at the Neighborhood Watch meeting it was brought
  up that a list should be published of City staff who are trained on equipment in the case of an
  emergency. CHAIR ROMANELLI volunteered to be involved in learning how to use emergency
  equipment. Community Services Director Clark stated that Daniel A-Haja has helped to put
  together emergency container that is Cat5/Cat6 wired in case the City needs to move into a
  temporary office.

15.  ADJOURNMENT

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ to,

  ADJOURN THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING AT 8:42 P.M. TO THE NEXT
  MEETING OF THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING SCHEDULED ON
  MONDAY, MARCH 19, 2018.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  _____________________________  _____________________________
  Carol Corea  Heidi Luce
  Administrative Assistant  City Clerk
